BunFrame RSC — design notes (v2)
================================

This file records design decisions and what was deliberately deferred. v1
landed RSC + client-side soft-nav. v2 added module-level Server Functions
with `<form action>` and `useActionState` plumbing. The structure of the
file is the same: each section is a feature, with what we shipped, what we
didn't, and why.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1) Single process, --conditions react-server, NO server-side HTML pre-render
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
What we ship now:
  - server.ts boots under `bun --conditions react-server`
  - The router renders only the RSC payload (Pass 1)
  - The HTML response is a small shell with the RSC payload embedded inline
    in <script type="text/x-component" id="__BUNFRAME_RSC__">
  - The browser reads that payload, deserializes it via
    react-server-dom-webpack/client.browser, and mounts with createRoot()

What we DON'T do yet:
  - No HTML pre-render of the React tree on the server.

Why: in a single Node/Bun process running under the `react-server` export
condition, both `react-dom/server` and `react-dom/static` resolve to a stub
that throws "not supported in React Server Components" (verified in
node_modules/react-dom/server.react-server.js and static.react-server.js).
React expects two runtimes: one for the RSC pass (server-only React, this
condition) and one for the SSR pass (regular React, no condition). Doing
both in one process needs either a worker_thread, a child process, or a VM
context with separate module resolution. That's a sizable engineering
project and was deliberately deferred.

Tradeoff: First Contentful Paint is slightly worse — the browser sees an
empty <div id="root"> until the inline RSC payload is parsed and rendered.
For most pages the payload is in the same HTML response so the delay is
small (no extra round trip).

How to add it later:
  - Spawn a worker on boot that imports React/react-dom/server WITHOUT the
    react-server condition, plus the client manifest. Pipe the RSC stream to
    the worker; it returns a stream of HTML.
  - Or: spawn the worker per-request (slower start, simpler lifecycle).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2) Client-side navigation — DONE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Soft-navigation is in. Two new pieces and a router branch:

  - router.ts: when `Accept: text/x-component`, the route handler returns the
    raw renderToReadableStream body with `Content-Type: text/x-component`
    and `X-Bunframe-Params: <json>`. No HTML shell. Same URL as the page
    request — header-only switch, so the cache key matches HTML (no _rsc=1
    query param polluting the URL bar or breaking shareable links).

  - framework/client-router.ts: navigate(href) and a popstate listener.
    Updates window.__PARAMS__ from X-Bunframe-Params before the body
    finishes streaming so client components calling useParams() see the
    new values, not stale ones.

  - framework/Link.tsx ("use client"): renders a plain <a>, but on a primary
    same-origin click without modifier keys / target / download, it
    preventDefault()s and calls navigate(). External / target=_blank /
    download / modifier-key clicks fall through to native <a> behavior.

The setRoot setter (formerly held in client-router.ts) now lives in
framework/rsc/call-server.ts. Both navigation and Server Function calls
swap the live tree through that one setter — single source of truth.

Deliberately not done: scroll restoration, prefetch on hover, view
transitions, pending-state UX, type-checked routes. Add when actually needed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3) Server Functions ("use server", module-level) — DONE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Every export of a "use server" file becomes a Server Function: callable from
client components, callable as a `<form action>`, integrates with
useActionState. Module-level only — inline closures (`function() { "use server"; ... }`
inside a server component) are NOT supported in this pass; see §7.

Wire shape:

  ID             ${absPath}#${exportName} — same scheme manifest.ts uses for
                 client refs. Stable across restarts on the same disk.
                 No content hashing, no key registry to maintain.

  Endpoint       The page route handles BOTH GET and POST. POSTing to the
                 route is "call a Server Function in the context of this
                 page". This matches Next.js's shape (POST to current URL +
                 header) and lets us re-render the route in the same response.

  JS-driven      Client's callServer (in framework/rsc/call-server.ts) sets
                 `X-Bunframe-Action-Id: <id>` and posts an encodeReply()
                 body. Server: lookup fn by id (lazy `await import(absPath)`),
                 decodeReply args, await fn(...args), then re-render the
                 route. Response is a flight stream encoding
                 { returnValue, root }. Client puts returnValue back to the
                 caller and swaps the live tree to root — so every action
                 transparently refreshes the page.

  Form submit    `<form action={fn}>` works without JS. React serializes
                 action metadata into FormData fields ($ACTION_REF_*,
                 $ACTION_ID_*). Server uses decodeAction(formData,
                 serverManifest) to recover the bound function call,
                 decodeFormState for useActionState, then renders HTML —
                 same shell shape as a GET, with formState plumbed through
                 renderToReadableStream's options so useActionState reads
                 the right value on the next render.

  Cross-boundary When a server component passes a server fn as a prop to a
                 client component, the encoder needs to recognize the fn as
                 a reference. The runtime plugin appends
                 `registerServerReference(fn, absPath, name)` to every
                 "use server" file at server-side load time, so the function
                 carries the right $$typeof/$$id metadata.

  Browser stubs  Bun.build's plugin (build-client.ts → makeUseServerStubPlugin)
                 replaces every "use server" file with createServerReference
                 calls. Without this, real server code would land in the
                 browser bundle — a security hole. The runtime plugin from
                 framework/rsc/plugin.ts is global to the Bun process, but
                 verified empirically that Bun.build does NOT inherit
                 globally-registered plugins, so the two pipelines stay
                 cleanly separate.

  Server shims   rsdw/server.edge calls __webpack_require__ /
                 __webpack_chunk_load__ on globalThis when resolving server
                 references during decodeAction. server-fn.ts'
                 installServerWebpackShims hangs Bun-native dynamic imports
                 off those globals, keyed by absPath.

What was reused: parseFnId / serverFnId mirror the client-ref id scheme.
ClientManifest type is reused for the server-reference manifest (same
{ id, chunks, name, async } shape).

What was deliberately cut from v1:
  - default exports of "use server" files are skipped. Use named exports.
    Adding default support means generating a binding for an anonymous
    expression, which we can't do without a real AST pass. Documented in
    server-fn.ts comments.
  - $$bound encryption — only meaningful when we have inline closures. See §7.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4) HMR — NOT in this pass
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
`bun --watch` restarts the whole process on file change in dev. That's
correct but slow. True RSC HMR has three moving parts (client-build chunk
swap, RSC payload re-fetch, React state preservation) — out of scope here.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5) Files removed during the v1 pass
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - app/(test)/api/[name]/{page,test}.tsx  (route-system experiments)
  - app/[id]/[name]/page.tsx               (route-system experiments)
  - index.html                             (router now generates the shell
                                            inline; was previously served
                                            via Bun's HTML import to inject
                                            hashed script tags)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6) Layout
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  framework/rsc/directives.ts    Directive scanner (skips //, /* */, BOM,
                                 multiple "use strict"/etc. before
                                 "use client"/"use server")
  framework/rsc/manifest.ts      Client-reference manifest (state + stub
                                 source generator)
  framework/rsc/server-fn.ts     Server Function id helpers, server-reference
                                 manifest, browser-stub generator,
                                 server-side wrapper appendix, and the
                                 globalThis __webpack_* shim installer.
  framework/rsc/call-server.ts   Browser-only. The callServer singleton that
                                 every server-reference proxy posts through;
                                 also holds the React setRoot used by both
                                 navigation and action auto-rerender.
  framework/rsc/scan.ts          Walks app/, components/, framework/ at
                                 startup; collects "use client" AND
                                 "use server" files.
  framework/rsc/plugin.ts        Bun runtime plugin: replaces "use client"
                                 modules with client-reference stubs and
                                 appends registerServerReference to
                                 "use server" modules. Global to the server
                                 process; does NOT bleed into Bun.build.
  framework/rsc/build-client.ts  Bun.build for the browser graph. A
                                 build-local plugin (makeUseServerStubPlugin)
                                 replaces "use server" files with
                                 createServerReference stubs. Returns both
                                 the client and server reference manifests.
  framework/router.ts            Page routes return { GET, POST }. GET
                                 renders to RSC and either embeds in HTML
                                 or returns raw. POST handles two action
                                 dispatch paths (X-Bunframe-Action-Id +
                                 multipart form), then re-renders and
                                 returns { returnValue, root } (or HTML
                                 with formState plumbed through).
  framework/client-router.ts     Browser-side router. navigate(href) and
                                 popstate; uses the shared setRoot from
                                 call-server.ts.
  framework/Link.tsx             "use client" link component.
  client.ts                      Reads the inline RSC payload, lifts it into
                                 Root state so both navigation and actions
                                 can swap it, and mounts via createRoot.
  server.ts                      Boots: register plugin → install server
                                 webpack shims → scan → build client →
                                 start serving.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7) Inline "use server" closures — NOT in this pass; full sketch
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
This is the biggest piece of Server Functions parity that we deliberately
skipped. Here's the plan in enough detail that whoever picks it up next
doesn't have to re-derive it.

Goal:

    export default function Page({ userId }) {
      async function deletePost(postId) {
        "use server";
        await db.deletePost({ userId, postId });
      }
      return <Form action={deletePost} />;
    }

`deletePost` closes over `userId`. It has to be:
  (a) liftable to module scope so it has a stable identity to assign an ID
  (b) callable from the client without leaking userId in plaintext

The transform (compile time):

  1. Find every function whose body's first statement is `"use server"`.
     Function declarations, function expressions, and arrow functions. Also
     class methods if we want to be thorough.

  2. For each such function, compute its FREE VARIABLES — every identifier
     read in the body that isn't bound locally. Local bindings include:
       - parameters and destructured parameter patterns
       - var/let/const declarations and their destructuring
       - inner function declarations
       - catch clause bindings
       - for/for-in/for-of loop variables
       - class declarations and their methods
       - imports (these are "free" but should be kept as imports, not bound)
     Module-scope identifiers and unresolved references should be passed
     through (they'll be available in the lifted function too).

  3. Lift the function to module scope. Generate a stable ID via SHA-256
     over the lifted source (matches Next.js's content-hash approach).

       async function $$action_<hash>(__userId, postId) {
         /* original body, with `userId` rewritten to `__userId` if needed —
            but if the original name doesn't shadow anything we can just
            keep it: `async function $$action_<hash>(userId, postId) { ... }` */
       }
       registerServerReference($$action_<hash>, "<hash>", null);

  4. Replace the original site with a bound reference:

       const deletePost = $$action_<hash>.bind(null, userId);

     React's flight encoder serializes a function with $$bound as a server
     reference; the client sees it as a callable that POSTs id + bound args.

  5. Encrypt the bound args. Without this, the client can read userId off
     the wire (info leak) AND submit a request with userId substituted
     (privilege escalation — the server would happily run deletePost as
     someone else).

       - Per-process AES-GCM key. Bun has Web Crypto natively.
       - Key in memory only by default. Restart invalidates in-flight
         encrypted bound args; acceptable.
       - For multi-instance deployments, env var BUNFRAME_ACTION_KEY
         (base64 of 32 random bytes). Document.
       - Encrypt at the encoding boundary (when we serialize bound args
         out), decrypt at the decoding boundary (when decodeReply hands
         them back to us).

AST tooling — we currently use Bun.Transpiler.scan (exports only). For step
2 we need real scope analysis. Options:
  - oxc-parser (Rust core, npm package). Fast, has scope info. Recommended.
  - @swc/core. What Next.js uses. Heavy, but well-trodden.
  - Babel. Slower; ergonomic plugin API. Probably overkill.
  - Hand-rolled. Don't.

What it touches:
  - framework/rsc/inline-server-fn.ts (NEW): the AST pass + crypto helpers.
  - framework/rsc/plugin.ts: invoke the AST pass before the existing
    "use server" branch. The branch already records server modules and
    appends registerServerReference; the inline pass adds new top-level
    declarations whose ids the appendix should also register.
  - framework/rsc/build-client.ts: the makeUseServerStubPlugin needs to
    handle inline-lifted ids. Since they're now module-level
    declarations, the existing stub generator works — just feed it the
    id list from the AST pass alongside the file's regular exports.

Non-negotiable: when this lands, $$bound encryption MUST land with it.
No "v1 without crypto" — that's a real privilege-escalation hole, not a
nice-to-have.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8) Things still missing for "would I ship it for real"
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Honest list, roughly priority order:
  - SSR pre-render (§1) — biggest user-visible win (FCP).
  - HMR (§4) — DX.
  - Inline "use server" (§7) — Next.js parity.
  - Revalidation primitives (revalidatePath / revalidateTag / cache).
  - Metadata API (head, title, fonts).
  - useActionState progressive-enhancement: we plumb formState through but
    haven't end-to-end tested a no-JS submit with state preservation. The
    JS path works; the no-JS path needs an integration test before it can
    be claimed.
